skills.packageGuideCopyFailed: Copy failed. Expand the prompt and copy it manually.
skills.packageGuidePrompt:
Package this Skill as a SourceLens-compatible zip. Follow every requirement below.

1. Package layout
- The archive itself, or exactly one top-level directory, must be the Skill root.
- The Skill root must contain exactly one SKILL.md. It may also contain sourcelens.json, scripts/, bin/, references/, and other runtime resources.
- Do not include .git, .ssh, __pycache__, node_modules, .venv, symlinks, device files, credentials, build caches, or parent/absolute paths.

2. SKILL.md
- Save it as UTF-8 and begin with closed YAML frontmatter containing name and description.
- name must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,179}$ and should be a stable slug.
- Explain when the Skill applies, which bundled resources it uses, and what the Agent should do with each. Reference bundled executables by their path relative to the Skill root, for example bin/linux-amd64/income, and declared Transforms by their stable name; do not invent or search for paths at runtime. Do not name runtime execution tools in SKILL.md: SourceLens automatically exposes the matching tool for each declared executable and Transform.
- State the supported operating systems and CPU architectures. SKILL.md must be no larger than 256 KB.

3. Environment and HTTP policy
- Declare environment variable metadata in sourcelens.json at the Skill root. Never package variable values or secrets.
- Variable names must match ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$ and be unique. Each item supports name, description, required, and secret.
- If the Skill uses call_skill_api, add the smallest required api allowlist. base_url_env must reference a declared environment variable; each route must declare either path or path_prefix and allowed methods.

4. Executable files
- Put native executables under bin/, conventionally bin/linux-amd64/ and bin/linux-arm64/. Scripts go under scripts/.
- run_skill_script executes one file per call, resolved relative to the Skill root. A shebang, a .py suffix, or a .sh suffix selects the interpreter automatically; any other file (such as a native binary) must carry an execute bit to run. Set every file you intend to run to 0755 before creating the zip.
- Files without an execute bit are not runnable. Do not add a wrapper that searches bin/, runs chmod, or executes an arbitrary path.
- run_skill_script has a per-run call budget. Raw stdout and stderr are streamed under per-call and per-run byte quotas. The tool returns a bounded preview and typed synopsis; in SKILL.md, direct the Agent to prefer one bounded bulk call and analyze saved stdout_ref results with inspect_saved_output or analyze_structured_output instead of fanning out per-record calls.

5. LensNode runtime compatibility
- The standard Linux LensNode image is Debian 12 (bookworm), Python 3.12, and glibc 2.36. A selected node may use x86_64/amd64 or aarch64/arm64; do not assume amd64.
- When the target node is available, record uname -s, uname -m, /etc/os-release, and ldd --version before building. If the target is not fixed, bundle and test both Linux architectures. Prefer statically linked binaries; otherwise build against libraries no newer than the target runtime and document required dynamic libraries.
- Do not download or compile executables during a Run. Do not depend on a repository checkout, package manager, architecture-specific loader, or fixed working directory.

6. Permissions and verification
- Set intended script and native executable files to 0755 before creating the zip, and create the archive with a tool that preserves Unix mode metadata. SourceLens sanitizes restored modes and re-enables execute permission for files under scripts/ and for any other file that already carries an execute bit.
- Verify file format and architecture with file, dependencies with ldd when applicable, and archive modes/layout with zipinfo -l.

7. Upload limits
- Zip size: at most 50 MB. Unpacked total: at most 100 MB.
- Each file: at most 50 MB. File count: at most 300.
- Test every bundled executable for the target OS/CPU before upload and ensure an unsupported platform fails without falling back to another binary.

settings.publicBaseUrlDesc: Base address used for assistant share links (e.g. your own domain). Leave empty to use the current server address.
settings.nodeImageDesc: Docker image used in the generated compose. Leave empty to use the default oneprolabs/lensnode:latest.
settings.timeoutDesc: Default timeout for LensNode task execution.
settings.retentionDesc: How many days to keep Runs and execution records before cleanup.
settings.offlineDesc: If no heartbeat is received within this many seconds, health checks mark the node offline.
settings.cleanupIntervalDesc: Execution interval for the LensNode cleanup task, in seconds.
settings.healthIntervalDesc: Execution interval for the LensNode health check task, in seconds.
settings.retentionIntervalDesc: Execution interval for the run retention cleanup task, in seconds.
settings.skillGeneratorModelDesc: Default LLM configuration used when SourceLens generates Workspace Guide Skills. Leave empty to use template-only generation.
settings.smartCollaborationModelDesc: Interprets requests, selects available assistants, and coordinates collaboration. Required for Smart Collaboration conversations.

resourceSettings.syncTimeoutDesc: Maximum time SourceLens waits for LensNode to finish a data source sync. It is also used as the sync lock TTL.
resourceSettings.syncWorkersDesc: Platform-level global default. It controls the maximum number of concurrent workers each datasource sync task can use inside LensNode. It mainly affects Feishu folder scanning, file downloads, and conversion preparation; Git sync is usually affected less. Higher values may improve sync speed, but increase Feishu API requests, local CPU/memory usage, and model conversion pressure.
resourceSettings.visionModelDesc: Default model for image descriptions, embedded document images, and PDF advanced recognition when a datasource does not override it.
resourceSettings.documentModelDesc: Default model for future model-enhanced document conversion when a datasource does not override it. Normal text extraction does not call it today.

datasourceWizard.conversionHint: Generate searchable Markdown after sync and store outputs beside source files.
datasourceWizard.documentContentHint: Extract document text and optionally enrich it with embedded images or scanned PDF pages.
datasourceWizard.convertDocumentsHint: Extract text from PDF, DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX into Markdown.
datasourceWizard.documentModelHint: Optional. Leave empty to inherit the default document model from resource settings. Normal text extraction still uses the local converter today.
datasourceWizard.documentModelTooltip: Datasource-level override for the default document model. It is intended for future complex document understanding, structure enhancement, and model-based conversion. MarkItDown text extraction does not call it today.
datasourceWizard.standaloneImagesHint: Process image files in the datasource directory. This does not include images embedded inside documents.
datasourceWizard.convertImagesHint: Use a vision model to create searchable descriptions. This consumes model calls.
datasourceWizard.visionModelHint: Optional. Leave empty to inherit the default vision model from resource settings. If neither is configured, image recognition is skipped.
datasourceWizard.visionModelTooltip: Datasource-level override for the default vision model. It affects standalone images, embedded document images, and PDF visual recognition.
datasourceWizard.convertEmbeddedImagesHint: Requires document extraction. Describes images embedded in Office/PDF documents.
datasourceWizard.pdfAdvancedHint: PDF image recognition calls the vision model. By default it only complements weak-text/scanned pages to avoid indexing meaningless logos and icons.
datasourceWizard.pdfExtractImagesHint: Only controls image recognition inside PDF files. By default, it prioritizes larger images on scanned or image-based pages, then filters and compresses them before description.
datasourceWizard.pdfExtractImagesOnTextPages: Recognize images on normal PDF text pages
datasourceWizard.pdfExtractImagesOnTextPagesHint: Off by default. When enabled, pages that already have extractable text are still checked for images. Use this for documents with diagrams or flowcharts; it can increase cost and may describe logos, icons, or unrelated decorative images.
datasourceWizard.pdfRenderScannedPagesHint: When enabled, PDF pages without extractable text are sent to the vision model as rendered page images. Confirm the cost is acceptable.
datasourceWizard.pdfMaxPagesTooltip: Only limits PDF advanced recognition pages. It does not affect normal document text extraction.
datasourceWizard.pdfMaxImagesPerPageTooltip: Limits how many embedded images can be described per PDF page to avoid excessive calls on image-heavy pages.
datasourceWizard.pdfRenderDpiTooltip: Resolution for rendering scanned pages. Higher values are clearer but produce larger images and higher cost.
datasourceWizard.pdfMinTextCharsTooltip: Unit is characters. For example, 30 means that if a page has fewer than 30 directly extractable characters, SourceLens treats it as a possible scanned or image-based page. If full scanned-page recognition is enabled, the page is then recognized with the vision model.
datasourceWizard.pdfMinImageAreaRatioTooltip: Enter a page area ratio from 0 to 1, not pixels. For example, 0.08 means about 8%; images smaller than 8% of the page are skipped to filter logos, icons, and decorative images.
datasourceWizard.conversionLimitsHint: Keep conversion bounded for large files and image-heavy datasources.
datasourceWizard.globalConversionLimitsHint: Bound all conversion inputs. PDF-specific page and image-density limits are configured under PDF advanced recognition.
datasourceWizard.maxFileSizeTooltip: Source files larger than this value are skipped by conversion to avoid slowing down sync tasks.
datasourceWizard.maxImagesTooltip: Limits the total number of images described in one task, including standalone images and embedded document images.

wizard.contextPlaceholder:
# Information the model can't know just from reading code — write it here.

## Project overview
# SourceLens is a self-hosted AI code Q&A platform.
# backend/ is the Django REST API; lensnode/ is a separately deployed execution node
# that runs Deep Agents and pushes results back to the main service via WebSocket.
# frontend/ is the Vue 3 admin console; it only talks to backend/ REST APIs.

## Search priorities
# Business logic lives in backend/lens/. backend/agentcore/ is a git submodule — don't look for business code there.
# Frontend pages: frontend/src/pages/lens/. Admin components: frontend/src/admin/.
# Agent behavior: lensnode/lensnode/agent_runtime.py.

## Avoid misreading
# references/ contains reference documents, not source code — don't analyze it as code.
# For current field structure, read the latest migration only, not historical ones.
